description: IPC surface for the main window, which normally loads the loopback backend over HTTP and may load the bundled recovery page if the backend exits before startup. Exposes opener:open_url scoped to https URLs, the updater_state / run_binary_update / run_self_update commands, and the narrowly scoped quit_after_backend_failure recovery action. Nothing else is reachable from the page. The remote.urls wildcard port is required because the backend binds an OS-chosen loopback port; the shell's on_navigation guard (lib.rs) confines the normal webview to that single backend origin. Local access applies only to the trusted bundled recovery page created by the shell. The opener allow-list stays https://* (not per-broker hosts) deliberately: the sole caller is the broker OAuth flow with a backend-issued authorise URL, the backend is the app's own trust anchor, and enumerating each broker's authorise host here would silently break every newly added OAuth broker until a desktop rebuild.
